note_tweet.text:
how to not get locked out of your ai plan this month

grok bot cut usage over halloween weekend with no notice. one $300/month user's meter went 50% → 100% overnight with idle bots. openai merges chatgpt + codex limits in december. anthropic rewrote its plans the same week.

the play: find your meter > kill idle agents > know the fine print > set a reset reminder

> step 1: find your meter
- claude: go to https://t.co/SyyJ3sbZqp → settings → usage. two bars, 5-hour and weekly
- chatgpt: go to https://t.co/z4O8rSNSjj → settings → usage. from december one number covers chat and codex. official page: https://t.co/jEHqb0NAi7
- grok bot: the usage bar in the bot app. this is the one that jumped for people this weekend

> step 2: kill what you wouldn't pay for
- list every routine, scheduled task, or always-on agent you have
- ask: would i pay api prices for this to run at 3am? if no, pause it

> step 3: know the fine print
- anthropic ultra ($200): no 5-hour limit, but only for verified accounts. newer accounts keep a temporary cap until an email says it's lifted. weekly cap stays
- openai: "virtually unlimited" instant chat is only stated for the business plan
- grok: musk said serving cost was "unsustainably high relative to revenue." pools were adjusted after the fact

> step 4: set a reset reminder
- every meter shows a reset time next to it. put the weekly one in your calendar. plan heavy runs right after it, not right before

> the catch
- none of these plans publish a token price. your meter is the only truth
- a plan can change mid-month. three did this week

> what not to do
- don't assume $200 means unlimited. it never has
- don't leave an agent loop running overnight on a flat plan

treat the meter like a bank balance, not a feature.

reply with your plan and what you run overnight, and i'll tell you which limit bites first.

bookmark this and open it in december.

article.title: Every coding agent has a meter now. Here's how to stop wasting yours

data.text: Claude dropped the 5-hour limit. ChatGPT and Codex share one pool in December. Grok Bot ran out early this week. https://t.co/fVXKakxGRo

note_tweet.text:
这条推文来自 OpenAI 团队核心成员 Tibo（@​thsottiaux），他在 Codex、ChatGPT Work 及 Agent 系列产品的推进中扮演关键角色。推文的核心是宣布 OpenAI 的常驻式主动智能体产品“dots”正在接入包括 GPT-6 Astra 和 GPT-6.1 Terra 在内的多模型矩阵。

具体拆解与客观分析如下：

---

■ 一、 关键术语与背景

• Fellow resetters（重置党们）：社区黑话。Tibo 常在 X 上宣布 Codex / Work 的额度重置（Reset），社区甚至有专门的重置追踪站点，因此他习惯将等待额度刷新的用户和开发者群体称为“resetters”。
• dots：OpenAI 推出的一款常驻、主动型智能体（Proactive / Always-on Agent），旨在跨越日常项目与多应用环境自主跟进并执行任务，而非单次的问答交互。
• GPT-6 Astra：定位为重型旗舰前沿模型，擅长高难度逻辑推演、深度代码重构与复杂规划，但推理时延和算力成本较高。
• GPT-6.1 Terra：定位为快速、高效的高性价比前沿模型，在保持精准视觉推理与计算机操作能力的同时，显著提升了响应速度和自然表达。

---

■ 二、 推文表达的核心动向

1. 摆脱单一模型依赖，走向分级调度  
   智能体如果全程使用超大旗舰模型（如 Astra），往往会出现交互等待时间过长、后台常驻成本过高的问题。引入 Terra 代表 dots 正转向“多模型分层架构”：重活深度任务分配给高算力基座，轻快交互与实时协作交给高效模型。

2. 改善交互体感（速度 + 人格）  
   常驻助手最忌讳机械迟钝。Terra 主打低时延与更自然的表达（Personality upgrade），使 dots 在与用户共同工作时的沟通体验更像实时在线的协作伙伴，而非卡顿的命令行工具。

3. 降低边际成本，推进大规模下沉  
   “bring dots to more people”意味着降低部署成本。使用轻量高效的 Terra 能够显著压降单次交互与后台轮询的算力消耗，为未来向更广泛的订阅层级甚至免费用户群开放打下基础。

---

■ 三、 需要注意的变量与潜在成本

• 速度提升背后的能力折中：高效模型往往在极端边界场景（极长代码链路推理、高歧义约束判断）中不如顶级推理旗舰严密。实际体验高度取决于官方在任务分发路由（Routing）上的判断机制。
• “个性升级”在生产环境的双刃剑：对生产力工具而言，过于活跃或拟人化的表达若处理不当，可能伴随更多废话或迎合式幻觉，影响实际自动化流的确定性。
• 开放节奏与配额限制：虽然声称覆盖更多人群，但常驻 Agent 带来的长上下文与持续计算压力依然很大，实际开放节奏可能依然受限于分批灰度与并发额度控制。

---

Here’s the grok summary:

Partly yes — it was a confirmed glitch (dashboard/metering issue), with a separate cost-related factor.
On November 1, 2026, many Grok Bot (@bot) users reported sudden jumps to 100% (or near it) on their weekly usage meters, often with bots idle or only minimal activity. Some meters flipped in real time (e.g., between ~77% and 100%).
This aligned with a Billing and Usage Dashboard degradation reported on https://t.co/BDQCe9l2O9. Official Grok responses and Cursor support (who handle related Grok Bot issues) noted that such sharp jumps without matching work shouldn’t happen and that the incident could produce inaccurate full-usage readings. The dashboard issue was investigated and later marked resolved; the status page currently shows no active incidents.
Separately, Elon Musk posted in response to users asking for resets: “The cost of serving Grok Bot was unsustainably high relative to revenue.” This pointed to underlying cost pressure (Grok Bot is resource-intensive as an always-on agent). Some users later saw meters drop (e.g., 100% → ~50% or similar corrections), and there were earlier similar reports in mid-October that Musk said he was looking into.
In short: the sudden idle spikes to 100% were largely a confirmed metering/display glitch that has been addressed. Tighter effective limits for some users also appear tied to the high serving costs Musk mentioned. Check Settings → Usage & Billing in the app for your current reading and reset time, and contact support@x.ai with screenshots if the numbers still don’t match your actual use.
